title: The face of the real is covered by a golden vessel
theme: The first of the four closing prayers: the seeker asks Pūṣan to uncover the face of the real so that it may be seen.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «हिरण्मयमिव हिरण्मयम् , ज्योतिर्मयमित्येतत्» — ‘golden’ as if golden, that is, made of light

words.meaning: by a vessel, a bowl (or its lid)
words.context: Śaṅkara: «पात्रेणेव अपिधानभूतेन», a vessel serving as a lid; Mahīdhara: the sun’s disk, «पात्रं मण्डलम्»

words.meaning: of the true, of the real
words.context: Śaṅkara: Brahman in the sun’s disk; Deśika: the individual self («सत्यशब्दोऽत्र जीवपरः»); Madhva: Viṣṇu («विष्णोः सत्यस्य»)

words.gram: past passive participle, n. nom. sg.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «मुखं द्वारम्», ‘the door’; Mahīdhara: «मुखं शरीरम्»; Deśika: the mind, which stands like a face for the self

words.role: object of apāvṛṇu (refers to the covering, or to the face)
words.context: Śaṅkara: «तत् त्वं हे पूषन् अपावृणु अपसारय»
Śaṅkara (on mantra 16) explains the name from poṣaṇa, ‘nourishing’: the sun, who nourishes the world

words.gram: verb, root vṛ (5th class, P.), with apa and ā, imperative 2nd sg.
words.role: main verb of the second half

words.meaning: for one whose dharma is truth; (or) for the dharma of the true one
words.role: dative of the person for whom (or of what the uncovering serves)
words.context: Śaṅkara: «सत्यं धर्मो यस्य मम सोऽहं सत्यधर्मा तस्मै मह्यम्», ‘for me, whose dharma is truth’
Śaṅkara: «तव सत्यात्मन उपलब्धये», ‘so that I may reach you, the real’

sandhi.rule: a + a → ā: P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः). The final m of apihitam becomes anusvāra before the consonant of mukham: P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः).

t before t stays (tat tvam, written तत्त्वं); the m of tvam becomes anusvāra before p (P. 8.3.23 (मोऽनुस्वारः)). Written together, तत्त्वं can look like the abstract noun tattva, ‘thatness’; it is not.
A word-final n after a short vowel is doubled before a vowel: P. 8.3.32 (ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम्) — pūṣan + apāvṛṇu → pūṣann apāvṛṇu.

samasa.vigraha: सत्यं धर्मः यस्य सः — or — सत्यस्य धर्मः
samasa.meaning: one whose dharma is truth (the seeker); or: the dharma (attribute) of the true one

morphology.note: hiraṇmaya, ‘golden’, is one of the forms Pāṇini gives ready-made rather than by rule, in the list of P. 6.4.174 (दाण्डिनायनहास्तिनायनाथर्वणिकजैह्माशिनेयवाशिनायनिभ्रौणहत्यधैवत्यसारवैक्ष्वाकमैत्रेयहिरण्मयानि): from hiraṇya + -maya with the syllable ya lost.
api + √dhā ‘to put’: the participle of dhā is hita (P. 7.4.42 (दधातेर्हिः)); api-hita, ‘put over, covered’.
Imperative of vṛ ‘to cover’ (5th class, stem vṛṇu-) with apa ‘away’ and ā: ‘uncover’. The ending -hi is dropped after the u of the stem: P. 6.4.106 (उतश्च प्रत्ययादसंयोगपूर्वात्).

An a-stem dative. If the compound is a bahuvrīhi, as Śaṅkara takes it (he calls the person satyadharmā), classical grammar would turn dharma into dharman at the end of it — P. 5.4.124 (धर्मादनिच् केवलात्) — and give the dative satyadharmaṇe. The a-stem form fits a tatpuruṣa more naturally, as Deśika reads it; as a bahuvrīhi it is a Vedic form. Both readings are possible; the grammar alone does not decide.
Dative of dṛṣṭi, an action noun in -ti from dṛś (P. 3.3.94 (स्त्रियां क्तिन्)): the dative expresses purpose, ‘for seeing’.

anvaya: सत्यस्य मुखम् हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण अपिहितम् । पूषन् त्वम् सत्यधर्माय दृष्टये तत् अपावृणु ।
syntax: Two sentences. The first is a statement with a participle as its predicate: ‘the face of the real [is] covered by a golden vessel’. The second is a request in the imperative addressed to Pūṣan: ‘that, you, Pūṣan, uncover’, with two datives saying for whom and for what — satyadharmāya (for the one whose dharma is truth, or for the true one’s dharma) and dṛṣṭaye (for seeing). tat refers back to the face, or to what covers it; Śaṅkara takes it as the covering to be moved aside.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: Brahman dwelling in the sun’s disk («सत्यस्य आदित्यमण्डलस्थस्य ब्रह्मणः»). Deśika: the individual self, whose ‘face’ — the mind — is covered by the golden lid of passion (rajas). Madhva: Viṣṇu, the Real, whose face is covered by the sun’s disk («पात्रं हिरण्मयं सूर्यमण्डलं समुदाहृतम्»). The mantra names no one.

pātra is a drinking vessel or bowl. Śaṅkara reads it as a vessel used as a lid; Mahīdhara (on VS 40.17) derives it from ‘drinking’ and identifies it with the sun’s disk, where the rays drink the waters («पिबन्ति यत्र स्थिता रश्मयो रसानिति पात्रं मण्डलम्»); Deśika as the ‘golden’, that is, attractive, covering of passion.

‘For me, whose dharma is truth’ (Śaṅkara’s first gloss); ‘for one who practises dharma as it truly is’ (his second, «यथाभूतस्य धर्मस्यानुष्ठात्रे»); ‘for the sight that is the attribute of the true self’ (Deśika); ‘for the devotee’ (Madhva’s verse: «सत्यधर्माय भक्ताय»). See the morphology note on the form.

ambiguities.topic: The Mādhyandina form of this mantra
ambiguities.note: VS 40.17 keeps only the first line and continues ‘yo ’sāv āditye puruṣaḥ so ’sāv aham | om khaṃ brahma’ — ‘the person who is in the sun, that I am. Om, Brahman is space’. The request to Pūṣan is absent there (corrections.json, class recension).

metre.name: anuṣṭubh
metre.note: Two half-lines of 16 syllables. Mahīdhara classes the Mādhyandina form of the mantra (VS 40.17, which adds prose) as an uṣṇik ending in two yajus («उष्णिक् यजुर्द्वयान्ता»).

translation.literal: By a golden vessel the face of the real [is] covered. That, you, O Pūṣan, uncover, for [one] whose dharma is truth (or: for the dharma of the true), for seeing.
translation.readable: The face of the real is hidden by a golden vessel. Uncover it, Pūṣan, so that I, who hold to the truth, may see.

beginner: Here the Upanishad changes its voice. Until now it has taught; now it prays. The speaker imagines the truth as a face, and that face is hidden — not by something ugly, but by something golden and dazzling. That is the striking point: what hides the truth is beautiful. The prayer is addressed to Pūṣan, an old name for the sun as the one who nourishes and guides. ‘Open it,’ the speaker asks, ‘so that I can see.’ Teachers have read the golden cover in different ways: as the blazing disk of the sun itself, as the attractive surface of the world, or as our own desires, which glitter and keep our attention on the surface. What they share is the idea that seeing truly is not something we simply do; something has to be opened.
analogy: Think of sunlight on a window so bright that you cannot see into the room behind it: the glare is beautiful, and it is exactly what hides what is inside.

commentary.q: What does the mantra say, and to whom?
commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: It states that ‘the face of the real’ (satyasya mukham) is ‘covered’ (apihitam) by ‘a golden vessel’ (hiraṇmayena pātreṇa), and asks Pūṣan to uncover it ‘for one whose dharma is truth’ or ‘for the true one’s dharma’, ‘for seeing’. It is the first of four mantras in the voice of a petitioner; the teaching voice of mantras 1–14 does not return. The same four mantras, in the same order, close Bṛhadāraṇyaka 5.15.1, where they belong to the rites of the dying. Nothing in the words says who the speaker is, what ‘the real’ is, or what the golden vessel stands for.

commentary.q: Why does a prayer for a path come after the teaching on knowledge?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara’s introduction to this mantra joins it to mantras 11 and 14. The whole Veda has two aims, activity and withdrawal («द्विप्रकारः प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिलक्षणो वेदार्थोऽत्र प्रकाशितः»); the highest result of the path of works with meditation is still within saṃsāra, ending at dissolution into prakṛti, while knowledge of the Self is the result of renunciation. The person who has lived by works together with meditation on the lower Brahman, and meditated on the ‘true’ as the person in the sun and in the right eye (he quotes Bṛhadāraṇyaka 5.5.2), asks at the time of death for the door of entry: «सोऽन्तकाले प्राप्ते सत्यात्मानमात्मनः प्राप्तिद्वारं याचते». The prayer is therefore not, for Śaṅkara, the prayer of the knower of mantra 7, who needs no path, but of the meditator.

commentary.q: What covers the face of the real?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: For Śaṅkara the vessel is ‘golden as if golden, that is, luminous’ («हिरण्मयमिव हिरण्मयम् , ज्योतिर्मयमित्येतत्»), the radiance of the sun’s disk which hides the door to Brahman within it. Mahīdhara, on the Mādhyandina form, gives the same picture and adds an etymology: the disk is a pātra because there the rays ‘drink’ the waters. Deśika moves the image inward: the ‘face’ of the true self is the mind, and the golden lid is passion (rajas), golden because it attracts («रागात्मकतया हिरण्मयसदृशेन रजोमयेन पात्रेण»), which blocks the mind’s turning towards the Lord who is near in the heart. Madhva returns to the sun: the golden vessel is the solar disk, by which the face of Viṣṇu, the Real, is always covered, and which he himself, as Pūṣan, removes for his devotee.

commentary.q: Who is Pūṣan, and who is the satyadharman?
commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: Pūṣan is a Vedic deity of nourishment, roads and safe passage; in this mantra and the next he is addressed together with the sun, and Śaṅkara, commenting on the next mantra, identifies him with it: the sun, named Pūṣan because it nourishes the world. The petitioner describes himself, or his purpose, with satyadharmāya. Śaṅkara’s first reading makes it a bahuvrīhi, ‘for me, whose dharma is truth’, because the speaker has worshipped the true; his second, ‘for the one who performs dharma as it is’. Deśika reads it with dṛṣṭaye, ‘for the sight that is the dharma (attribute) of the true one’, the self. The a-stem form satyadharmāya sits more easily with Deśika’s tatpuruṣa than with a classical bahuvrīhi (see the morphology note); Vedic usage permits both.

advaita.text: The speaker is the meditator who combined works with meditation on the true (the person in the sun); at death he asks Pūṣan to remove the luminous covering of the door to Brahman in the solar disk, «दृष्टये तव सत्यात्मन उपलब्धये». This is the path of the meditator, not of the knower: for the knower of the Self ‘there is no going’ — Śaṅkara argues in his conclusion (after mantra 18) that if vidyā in mantra 11 meant Self-knowledge, the request for a door and a path in this mantra would make no sense.

visistadvaita.text: Mantras 15–18 are to be meditated on by one established in the knowledge of Brahman with its auxiliaries; Pūṣan and the other names denote the Supreme Self, directly or through the deity («पूषादिशब्दाः सर्वशब्दवाच्यं परमात्मानमनुसन्दधताम्»). ‘The true’ is here the individual self («सत्यशब्दोऽत्र जीवपरः»), its ‘face’ the mind, and the golden lid passion; the prayer asks the Lord, ‘whose nature is to nourish those who depend on him’, to remove the obstacle to meditation.

dvaita.text: The golden vessel is the sun’s disk, by which the face of Viṣṇu, the Real, is always covered («पात्रं हिरण्मयं सूर्यमण्डलं समुदाहृतम् । विष्णोः सत्यस्य तेनैव सर्वदाऽपिहितं मुखम्»); Viṣṇu himself, called Pūṣan because he is full (pūrṇa), reveals it to his devotee. Madhva gives this in verses he does not attribute in the surviving digital text, which has a gap at the end of the passage.

schools.disagreement: The schools divide on almost every noun: the real is Brahman in the sun (Śaṅkara), the individual self (Deśika) or Viṣṇu (Madhva); the golden vessel is the sun’s radiance (Śaṅkara, Mahīdhara, Madhva) or passion (Deśika); the speaker is a dying meditator (Śaṅkara) or a living devotee in meditation (Deśika, Madhva). They agree that the uncovering is a gift asked for, not an achievement.

parallels.note: The same mantra, word for word, opens the closing prayer of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka (5.15.1, Kāṇva), which goes on with mantras 16, 17 and 18. There it stands among the rites at the end of life.
The person in the sun’s disk, and in the right eye, is meditated on as ‘the true’ (satya). Śaṅkara quotes this passage in his introduction to mantra 15 to identify the ‘true’ whose face is covered.

parallels.quote: हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलम्
parallels.note: ‘In the highest golden sheath is Brahman, stainless, without parts.’ The same golden imagery, but in the Muṇḍaka the gold is the dwelling of Brahman rather than what hides it.

The Gītā’s ‘sun-coloured, beyond darkness’, in a verse on remembering the supreme at the time of death — the context of Īśā 15–18. Deśika uses the phrase ‘sun-coloured’ of the form the seeker asks to see in mantra 16.

contemporary.text: The golden lid is an image many readers recognise from their own screens: what keeps attention from what matters is rarely ugly; it is bright, rewarding and well designed. Deśika’s reading — the covering is the mind’s attraction itself — fits this most closely, but even Śaṅkara’s solar reading makes the same point: the radiance is the obstacle. The mantra does not ask the seeker to smash the vessel; it asks for it to be opened. This is a reflection on the teaching, not part of the commentarial tradition.

reflect.beginner: What is something bright and pleasant in your life that sometimes stops you from noticing something more important?
reflect.deeper: If what hides the real is itself golden, can the real be found by rejecting the beautiful — or only by seeing through it?
reflect.practice: Before opening an app or a screen today, pause once and ask: ‘What am I hoping to see?’ Write down three of your answers in the evening, without judging them.

references.text: Śaṅkara’s concluding discussion (Advaita Sharada unit IS_C01_I02) uses this mantra’s request for a door as evidence that mantras 9–11 do not speak of Self-knowledge.
Mahīdhara reads the Mādhyandina VS 40.17, which keeps only this mantra’s first line, as a meditation on the person in the sun: «सूर्यमण्डलस्थः पुरुषोऽहमेवेत्यभेदेन चिन्तयेत्».

flags.note: Madhva’s digital text breaks off (‘…’) after «सत्यधर्माय भक्ताय»; the rest of his gloss on this mantra could not be read.
Whether satyadharmāya is a bahuvrīhi (Śaṅkara) or a tatpuruṣa (Deśika) affects whether the mantra describes the petitioner; the edition’s literal translation gives both.
